metadata.title: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise - Cisco (Network Devices Platform) Analytics
metadata.description: Techniques and formal MITRE ATT&CK Detection Analytics scoped to MITRE's 'Network Devices' platform -- the platform value ATT&CK uses for router/switch/firewall device techniques; MITRE does not define a separate 'Cisco' platform. Extracted from the official MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise STIX dataset. Loaded by the Threat Detection Library app to show ATT&CK coverage for this library's Cisco-scoped content: the ESCU catalogue's 'Cisco Network', 'Cisco ASA', 'Cisco IOS XE', and 'Cisco SD-WAN' components (70 entries) plus the dedicated 62-entry Cisco Network Device catalogue (data/cisco-detections.json), which was built specifically to close the gap this file identified -- excludes 'Cisco Duo', 'Cisco Isovalent', and 'Cisco NVM', which are genuinely Cisco-branded but not Network Devices platform telemetry.

techniques.description: Adversaries may search local system sources, such as file systems, configuration files, local databases, virtual machine files, or process memory, to find files of interest and sensitive data prior to Exfiltration.

techniques.description: Adversaries may establish persistence by modifying RC scripts, which are executed during a Unix-like system’s startup. These files allow system administrators to map and start custom services at startup for different run levels. RC scripts require root privileges to modify.

techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation. techniques.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing command and control channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main command and control server.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
techniques.description: Adversaries may selectively delete or modify artifacts generated to reduce indications of their presence and blend in with legitimate activity. techniques.description: In addition to clearing system logs, an adversary may clear the command history of a compromised account to conceal the actions undertaken during an intrusion. Copying malware payloads to new locations may also be combined with [File Deletion](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004) to cleanup older artifacts.

After the sequence is completed, opening a port is often accomplished by the host based firewall, but could also be implemented by custom software.
